Title: Prof Lukoye Atwoli reappointed as Dean at AKU Medical College
NewsSummary: Prof Lukoye Atwoli has been reappointed for a second five-year term as the Dean of the  AKU Medical College, East Africa
NewsContent:
​Prof Lukoye Atwoli has been reappointed for a second five-year term as the Dean of the Aga Khan University’s (AKU) Medical College, East Africa, effective 1 August 2025.

Professor Atwoli joined AKU Medical College, East Africa as the Dean in 2020, amidst the COVID-19 pandemic, which placed the Medical College at the forefront of a global health crisis. Through his empathetic, consultative and disciplined leadership, Dean Atwoli has successfully navigated the Medical College in East Africa, elevating the institution to new heights of excellence in medical education and research.

During his first term, Dean Atwoli oversaw the launch of the undergraduate medical education program, incorporating interprofessional learning with the undergraduate nursing program. In addition, he focused on enhancing the quality of AKU’s postgraduate programs, leading to the establishment of two new Master of Medicine programs in Paediatrics & Child Health and Obstetrics & Gynaecology in Dar es Salaam.

“I am excited to have been reappointed as the Dean of the Medical College, East Africa for a second term,” said Prof Atwoli. “Over my next term, I will prioritise the attraction of high-quality faculty, particularly in biomedical sciences, to advance cutting-edge research. I aim to launch a MSc (Master of Science) in Population Health, followed by a PhD in Health Sciences. I also intend to develop a world-leading Academic Health Centre in tandem with School of Nursing and Midwifery, East Africa.”

In his role as the Dean, Prof Atwoli expanded the Medical College’s Clinical Fellowship programs from four to 12. Under his leadership, research among faculty has thrived, evidenced by a 35% increase in annual peer-reviewed publications over the past four years. Through Prof Atwoli’s efforts, the number and value of research grants and funding obtained by faculty members have increased exponentially.

Prof Atwoli leads and participates in mental health research both locally and globally. He was appointed by the President of Kenya as the inaugural Chair of the Board for Mathari National Teaching and Referral Hospital. He also serves as the Secretary-General of the African Association of Psychiatrists and President of the African College of Neuropsychopharmacology. 

In 2022, in recognition of his professional contributions to Kenya, Prof Atwoli was awarded one of the country’s highest national honours, the Moran of the Order of the Burning Spear (MBS). In the same year, Prof Lukoye was elected as an International Fellow of the American Psychiatric Association.

In 2023, Prof Atwoli was elected a member of the US National Academy of Medicine, recognizing his contributions to global health and mental health worldwide. He continues to serve as Co-Chair of the Board on Global Health at the National Academies.
